passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis is management’s perspective of our current financial condition and results of operations, and should be read in conjunction with “ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS” and “ITEM 8. FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND SUPPLEMENTARY DATA” included in this report. This discussion and analysis includes the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 and comparison between such years. The discussion for the year ended December 31, 2023 and comparison between the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023 have been omitted from this annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, as such information can be found in “ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS” in our annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, which was filed on February 26, 2025. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: You should carefully consider the following risk factors in addition to the other information included in this report. Each of these risks could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, and/or liquidity, as well as, in certain cases, the value of an investment in our securities. Although the risks are organized by headings and each risk is discussed separately, many are interrelated. BUSINESS, INDUSTRY, AND OPERATIONS RISKS Our financial results are affected by volatile margins, which are dependent upon factors beyond our control, including the prices we pay to acquire feedstocks and the market prices at which we can sell our products. Our financial results are affected by the margin (i.e., the difference) between our product prices and the prices for crude oil, corn, and other feedstocks that we purchase, which can vary greatly based on global and regional market conditions, as well as by type and class of product or feedstock. Historically, product margins have been volatile, and we believe they will continue to be volatile in the future. The prices we pay to acquire feedstocks and the market prices at which we can ultimately sell our products depend upon several factors, including global and regional supplies, inventory levels, and availability of and demand for feedstocks, liquid transportation fuels, and other products. These in turn depend on, among other things, global and regional production levels, or capacities of suppliers and competitors; operational costs and flexibility (including natural gas, electricity, and water availability and costs); transportation and logistics availability and costs; proximity and access to product and feedstock supplies and markets; economic activity and growth levels; U.S. and foreign relations (including tariffs, duties, sanctions, or other trade restrictions); political affairs; government regulations; and the events described in many of the other risk factors below. The ability of the members of the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and other petroleum-producing nations that collectively make up OPEC+ to agree on and to maintain crude oil price and production controls has also had, and is likely to continue to have, a significant impact on the market prices of crude oil and certain of our products. Although several refinery closures have recently been announced or are in process and others are expected in the future, there have also been recent additions to global refining capacity, which create risks and uncertainties related to product margins, volatility, and market perceptions of the refining industry. Regarding low-carbon fuels margins, see also, among other risk factors set forth below, “ The availability and prices of our feedstocks and other critical supplies expose us to risks, ” and “ We are subject to risks arising from the Renewable and Low-Carbon Fuel Programs, and other regulations, policies, international certifications, and standards impacting low-carbon fuels. ” Many of these factors are interrelated, beyond our control, can vary globally and regionally, and may change quickly, adding to market volatility, while others may have

credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably covers gross interest expense, with coverage near the sector median, while net leverage sits modestly above the sector median but remains within an investment-grade profile. The refining cash generation base, though cyclical, supports the current debt load and provides headroom against the next leverage threshold.

Liquidity is solid, with cash exceeding short-term obligations and a current ratio above the sector median. The debt maturity profile is well laddered, with no single year requiring material refinancing, and the revolver remains undrawn, providing backup liquidity for working capital swings typical of refining.

key_risks.text: Refining margins are highly volatile and driven by factors beyond management control, including crude oil differentials, OPEC+ production decisions, and global capacity additions. The risk-factor passage highlights that margin volatility directly affects financial results, and the multi-year decline in operating income illustrates this sensitivity, which could pressure cash flow if margins weaken further.

The debt note shows a substantial portion of public notes maturing in the near term, including senior notes due within the next few years. While the maturity ladder appears manageable, refinancing risk exists if credit markets tighten or if refining margins deteriorate, potentially increasing funding costs or limiting access to capital.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is adequate, with operating income covering gross interest expense multiple times, and operating cash flow provides a strong buffer. However, the absence of capital expenditure data prevents a full assessment of free cash flow after reinvestment, which is material for evaluating debt servicing capacity in a capital-intensive refining business.

Net leverage is moderate and sits above the sector median, but the indicative financial risk profile remains minimal. The company has significant headroom before breaching the next leverage threshold, and cash on hand covers a meaningful portion of debt, supporting debt servicing capacity even under moderate cash flow stress.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer maintains a solid credit profile, supported by substantial operating cash flow, adequate interest coverage, and a manageable debt maturity profile. Leverage is moderate and within an investment-grade range, though it sits above the sector median. The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, but refining margin volatility remains a key sensitivity.

Forward-looking, the credit view hinges on refining margin recovery and disciplined capital allocation. Shareholder distributions absorb a significant portion of operating cash flow, limiting deleveraging capacity. If margins remain weak, leverage could drift higher, but current headroom and liquidity provide a cushion. The missing capex data is a material gap for assessing free cash flow and debt reduction potential.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流穩健覆蓋總利息支出，覆蓋率接近行業中位數，而淨槓桿略高於行業中位數，但仍處於投資級別範圍。煉油現金產生基礎雖具週期性，仍支撐當前債務負擔，並為下一槓桿門檻提供緩衝空間。
流動性穩健，現金超過短期債務，流動比率高於行業中位數。債務到期結構分佈良好，並無任何單一年份需要重大再融資，且循環信貸仍未提取，為煉油業典型的營運資金波動提供備用流動性。

key_risks.text: 煉油利潤率高度波動，並受管理層無法控制的因素驅動，包括原油價差、OPEC+產量決定及全球產能增加。風險因素章節強調利潤率波動直接影響財務業績，而營運收入多年下降說明此敏感性，若利潤率進一步減弱，可能對現金流構成壓力。
債務票據顯示相當部分公開票據於短期內到期，包括未來數年內到期的優先票據。雖然到期結構看似可控，但若信貸市場收緊或煉油利潤率惡化，再融資風險仍然存在，可能增加融資成本或限制資本獲取。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率充足，營運收入覆蓋總利息支出數倍，且營運現金流提供強大緩衝。然而，缺乏資本開支數據，無法全面評估再投資後自由現金流，這對評估資本密集型煉油業務的債務償付能力至關重要。
淨槓桿適中且高於行業中位數，但指示性財務風險狀況仍為極低。公司在突破下一槓桿門檻前有顯著緩衝空間，且手頭現金覆蓋相當部分債務，即使現金流面臨中度壓力，仍支撐債務償付能力。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人維持穩健信用狀況，受大量營運現金流、充足利息覆蓋及可控債務到期結構支持。槓桿適中且處於投資級別範圍，儘管高於行業中位數。指示性財務風險狀況為極低，但煉油利潤率波動仍是關鍵敏感性。
前瞻而言，信用觀點取決於煉油利潤率復甦及紀律性資本配置。股東分派吸收營運現金流相當部分，限制去槓桿能力。若利潤率持續疲弱，槓桿可能偏高，但當前緩衝空間及流動性提供 cushion。缺失的資本開支數據是評估自由現金流及債務削減潛力的重大缺口。
